highlighted: Check whether an A/B test result is statistically significant

items.markdown:
You can test your experiment data online with the [A/B-Test Calculator - Power & Significance](https://abtestguide.com/calc/) or the [Free A/B Test Calculator by Speero](https://speero.com/ab-test-calculator).[[1]](https://abtestguide.com/calc/)[[2]](https://speero.com/ab-test-calculator)

### Required Inputs

To check statistical significance, you need these metrics for both your control (A) and your variation (B):

- **Visitors (Sample Size):** Total number of users or sessions exposed to each version.
- **Conversions:** Total number of target actions (e.g., clicks, sign-ups, purchases) for each version.
- **Confidence Level:** The threshold for certainty, which is set to **95%** (alpha α = 0.05) as the industry standard.[[1]](https://abtestguide.com/calc/)[[2]](https://www.omnisend.com/ab-testing-calculator/)[[3]](https://www.optibase.io/ab-test-significance-calculator)

### Key Output Metrics

- **Conversion Rate (CR):** Conversions ÷ Visitors for each variant.
- **Relative Lift:** Percentage change of B compared to A:(C R𝐵−C R𝐴)÷C R𝐴×1 0 0.
- **p-Value:** The probability that the observed difference happened by random chance. A value **below 0.05** means the result is statistically significant at the 95% confidence level.
- **Z-Score:** A test statistic measuring how many standard deviations the difference is from zero.[[1]](https://www.surveymonkey.com/learn/research-and-analysis/ab-testing-significance-calculator/)[[2]](https://www.pearson.com/channels/calculators/ab-test-significance-calculator)[[3]](https://statisticsfundamentals.com/calculators/ab-test/)[[4]](https://abtestguide.com/calc/)[[5]](https://www.optibase.io/ab-test-significance-calculator)

If you'd like, share your **visitor counts** and **conversions** for Variant A and Variant B, and I can help you calculate the conversion rates, relative lift, and significance status.
